scope: Read-only soil/container audit of all 734 seed records. No seeds or production settings changed.
methodology: All records checked against actual mobile selector vocabulary; specialist cases researched directly; exact botanical identity or explicit synonym required for NC State matching. Matching source availability is not a certified horticultural approval. Commercial mix labels are broad, conditional classes; material is not drainage.

systemic_findings.title: Growing medium taxonomy omits carnivorous, aquatic and no-soil cases
systemic_findings.recommended_correction: Add these distinct regimes rather than map them to visually nearest existing mix names.

systemic_findings.title: Peat-free is an attribute rather than a full recipe
systemic_findings.recommended_correction: Separate peat-free composition preference from drainage, aeration, acidity and nutrient properties.

systemic_findings.title: Container material cannot stand in for drainage and suitability
systemic_findings.recommended_correction: Record drainage/reservoir/mounting and pot dimensions separately; retain plastic/ceramic as options where appropriate. Do not replace them wholesale with terracotta.

findings.title: Air plant offered ordinary potting media
findings.issue: The definition offers cactus and general potting substrates for an air plant. This can lead to planting a species grown without soil into a root medium.
findings.recommended_correction: Offer a no-soil/mounted growing option, remove these ordinary soil recommendations, and describe support/air circulation rather than imply a conventional soil-filled pot.

findings.title: Aquatic plant mapped to houseplant compost
findings.issue: The soil trait mentions pond soil, but both selectable recommendations describe ordinary houseplant substrates.
findings.recommended_correction: Add an aquatic medium category (aquatic compost or suitable heavy loam) and an aquatic basket/container configuration. Do not substitute general indoor compost.

findings.title: Nepenthes medium is not described by current generic codes
findings.issue: The selectable codes do not specify a low-nutrient, airy pitcher-plant substrate; generic cactus, ericaceous or peat-free commercial mixes are not interchangeable with it.
findings.recommended_correction: Use a specialist carnivorous/Nepenthes medium choice describing an open sphagnum-based mix with suitable porous components. Peat-free status alone is insufficient.

findings.title: Acid-loving compost is not equivalent to carnivorous-plant medium
findings.issue: The soil trait partly captures acidity, but selectable ericaceous/peat-free codes omit the crucial low-nutrient requirement.
findings.recommended_correction: Add a specialist low-nutrient carnivorous medium option; do not present ordinary fertilized ericaceous compost as an equivalent. Preserve species-specific water requirements.

findings.title: Mexican butterwort incorrectly reduced to acid/cactus compost
findings.issue: Neither category states the nutrient-poor mineral-rich medium needed here. Treating this Mexican butterwort like an acid-bog carnivore also misses its seasonal succulent phase.
findings.recommended_correction: Use a specialist tropical Pinguicula medium choice without pre-added fertilizer, with airy mineral components; do not require ericaceous acidity. Keep it distinct from wet bog carnivores.

findings.title: Acid-loving recommendation contradicts preferred soil chemistry
findings.issue: An ericaceous alternative is highlighted although species guidance prefers neutral to alkaline humus-rich soil.
findings.recommended_correction: Remove acid-loving from the recommended alternatives; retain an appropriate humus-rich, freely draining general perennial/container mix.

findings.title: Unqualified generic alternative omits required acidity
findings.issue: The specialist acidic choice is present, but a generic alternative can also be selected with no acidity constraint. The alternatives are not equally safe as currently described.
findings.recommended_correction: Recommend the acidic/ericaceous choice, or explicitly qualify any generic mix by the required acidic chemistry before highlighting it. Do not assume all green-plant or multipurpose products are acidic enough.

findings.title: Peat-free alone does not describe an aquatic substrate
findings.issue: The existing trait says pond soil while the only selectable recommendation is a peat-absence label.
findings.recommended_correction: Represent aquatic/marginal growing conditions and suitable mineral/loam-based substrate explicitly; retain peat-free as a separate attribute rather than the recipe.

findings.title: Acidity guidance differs among authoritative sources
findings.issue: NC State lists alkaline conditions, RHS allows acid/neutral/alkaline, and Cornell permits acid to neutral. A single-source pH rule would falsely label every acid mix invalid.
findings.recommended_correction: Do not auto-change from a pH keyword match. Review the generic acid-loving recommendation in the context of a well-drained humus-rich mix and species provenance; record that acidity is not universally required.

findings.title: Pink quill needs a separate bromeliad-medium review
findings.issue: The current cactus/general soil choices are not justified by the recorded sources. It is an epiphyte, but must not be blindly treated like every soil-free Tillandsia species.
findings.recommended_correction: Review as Wallisia cyanea (accepted synonym used by the primary source); establish an airy bromeliad/epiphyte container recipe before changing recommendations.

findings.title: Slipper orchid treated as interchangeable with ericaceous mix
findings.issue: Orchid and acid-loving are different substrate categories. Specialist orchid guidance distinguishes terrestrial/lithophytic species and native substrates; the current alternative lacks this detail.
findings.recommended_correction: Have the species-specific Paphiopedilum recipe checked; do not recommend general ericaceous soil merely because the plant is an orchid.
